Let \(M=\begin{pmatrix}4&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\). Then
\[
M^n=\begin{pmatrix}a_{n+1}&a_n\\a_n&a_{n-1}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since \(\det M=-1\), we have
\[
a_{n+1}a_{n-1}-a_n^2=(-1)^n,
\]
so \(\gcd(a_n,a_{n+1})=1\).

For \(m>n\), using \(M^m=M^{m-n}M^n\) and taking the \((2,1)\)-entry,
\[
a_m=a_{m-n}a_{n+1}+a_{m-n-1}a_n.
\]
Thus any common divisor of \(a_m\) and \(a_n\) divides \(a_{m-n}\), and conversely any common divisor of \(a_{m-n}\) and \(a_n\) divides \(a_m\). Hence
\[
\gcd(a_m,a_n)=\gcd(a_{m-n},a_n).
\]
Iterating the Euclidean algorithm gives
\[
\gcd(a_m,a_n)=a_{\gcd(m,n)}.
\]

Now
\[
\gcd(1986,6891)=3.
\]
Therefore
\[
\gcd(a_{1986},a_{6891})=a_3=17.
\]
So the common divisors are \(1\) and \(17\).

\[
\boxed{1,17}
\]
